thread:
maya: heads-up — want a quick design review on the run inspector I sketched. goal: make tool calls + structured outputs readable at a glance without expanding every invocation.

oliver: nice. can you drop the image or a very short gif? faster to react to visual.

maya: pasted two frames below (very rough). main ideas: compact run row with 3-line summary, a chevron to expand, small inline badges for invoked tools (icon + short name), and a tiny diff icon if the schema output changed vs previous run. also an 'open definition' link to jump to function editor.

sam: love the badges. + a11y: make sure badges have text labels and keyboard focus. also color contrast for red/green status — use icons not only color.

maya: agree. thinking aria-label="invoked tool: transcribe" on badges and tooltip. keyboard: tab moves to badge group then arrow keys expand run details.

rui: question: when expanded, do we inline the full JSON output or show a structured view? inline big JSON is noisy for long outputs.

maya: plan is structured tree by default collapsed (key: value rows), with a small "view raw" button that opens the raw JSON in a modal. but quick copy-of-path and copy-value actions should be one click next to each field.

alisa: copy actions are great. also maybe add a "rerun with same inputs" button on the row — common ask from SEs debugging. would it be sticky per run?

maya: yeah, per run. small replay icon. if pressed we open the playground input pane prefilled and highlight which tool was invoked.

oliver: for function defs: can we show signature hover when you click "open definition"? like a mini popover showing params, example payload, and versions. no full nav away.

maya: yep — popover w/ small footer links: open in editor / pin to side. keeps context.

sam: accessibility nit: streaming token output needs aria-live so screen readers hear progress. also ensure the expand/collapse has aria-expanded and the chevron is reachable by keyboard.

maya: noted — aria-live for streaming area, aria-expanded for each run row. will add to the spec.

devex-bot: reminder — design review in #design-sync at 3pm today if you want wider feedback.

rui: another UX thought: when multiple tool calls occur in one run, show a small timeline stripe with ticks for each call; hovering shows a mini tooltip with call time and latency. helps spot slow calls.

maya: yes — timeline stripe + hover tooltips. we can also highlight the slowest call in red and link to invocation trace.

alisa: copy tweak: in run list, replace "Run ID" label with "Invocation" (shorter and less technical for some PMs).

oliver: layout debate: should run list default to dense or comfy? dense fits more runs; comfy better for touch devices. maybe a toggle for list density and remember per-user.

maya: will add a user-level preference — default dense for desktop, comfy for mobile.

sam: super-small thing: keyboard shortcut to jump to latest run (g then r?). helpful during active debugging.

maya: adding shortcut proposal: "d" to focus run list, "j/k" to move, "enter" to expand. will write up in the PR.

rui: performance question: rendering many expanded runs could be heavy — consider virtualization and only hydrate expanded rows on demand.

maya: yep we'll virtualize and lazy-render expanded content. noted for dev infra.

alisa: final: can we include a lightweight "regression marker" if structured output changes schema shape vs baseline? small yellow dot with tooltip "schema drift" and link to eval.

maya: love it. adding that to the spec. thanks all — I'll push an updated mock w/ a11y annotations and the timeline stripe before the design sync.

oliver: :thumbsup:

sam: :eyes:

maya: thanks — ping me if anything else comes up.
